subject.title: [Feature] Allow per-binding tool restrictions (tools.deny) in route/ACP bindings

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `bindings[].tools.allow/deny` contract for route/ACP bindings, and where should that policy compose in the existing tool-policy stack?
rationale: This is a new public config and authorization surface; code can show the missing field, but maintainers need to choose the precedence and security semantics before implementation.

options.title: Add a binding policy layer
options.body: Define `bindings[].tools` as a fully enforced layer in the resolved conversation capability profile or default policy pipeline, with schema/types/docs and upgrade-safe tests.

options.title: Keep policy channel-specific
options.body: Reject binding-level tools for now and clarify docs to use existing channel group/direct/sender or agent policy surfaces instead.

options.title: Defer to broader scoped-identity work
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on the broader conversation identity or per-session policy design so one public access-control model lands first.

recommendation.title: Add a binding policy layer
recommendation.body: Define `bindings[].tools` as a fully enforced layer in the resolved conversation capability profile or default policy pipeline, with schema/types/docs and upgrade-safe tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the current capability-profile foundation and the open follow-up identity-mode issue that frames the broader product/security direction.
